title: Statistical Analysis of the Phaistos Disc: A Computational Methodology for Phonetic Key Evaluation
description: A rigorous computational and statistical framework for evaluating competing phonetic key hypotheses for the Phaistos Disc (~1700 BCE). The study applies Blind Grid Testing across 10 candidate keys, Bonferroni-corrected Monte Carlo simulation (10,000 trials), Shannon entropy analysis, corpus-control testing against the AED-TEI Egyptian corpus (675,773 tokens), sensitivity analysis (105/105 perturbations significant), and cross-validation (Spearman ρ=0.779). Three key-independent findings are established: (1) the [Sign#36→Sign#11] bigram adjacency Z=10, p≈0, ratio=7.69×; (2) corpus-domain control Z=27.16 (theological) vs Z=−0.40 (administrative), confirming ritual text classification; (3) Sign #45 (solar rosette) appearing exclusively at spiral centers A31 and B30. The Luwian Hieroglyphic key (G_LUWIAN) achieves the highest score (523, p<0.0001), yielding a solar-water cosmological reading (Tiwat + watar) structurally parallel to the Egyptian Amduat. A negative control test (Z=1.99 on synthetic disc) establishes that token-level scores are frequency-driven (~94%); only the three key-independent pillars are presented as primary publishable claims. All code and data are released open-source for independent replication.
notes: This work is presented as a methodology paper, not a definitive decipherment. The key design circularity (researcher awareness of disc statistics) means findings are exploratory. Independent replication by a Luwianologist is required for confirmation.
